questions.heading: Only Some Solvers Take Indicator Constraints
questions.stem: A MathOpt model of a feeder plan has four rows added with add_indicator_constraint. On OR-Tools 9.15 it is solved with mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS. What happens?

options.text: HiGHS solves it, turning each indicator into a big-M row first
options.says: HiGHS does not take indicator constraints at all; the solve fails.

options.text: HiGHS solves it, leaving the four indicator rows out without a word
options.says: The solve does not run; an exception is raised.

options.text: The solve raises an error, and its real reason is on __context__
options.says: Right: an AttributeError is raised, and 'Highs does not support indicator constraints' is attached as __context__.

options.text: MathOpt refuses the four rows already while the model is built
options.says: MathOpt accepts indicator constraints into any model; the solver decides at solve time.

questions.heading: CP-SAT Enforces a Row Only When a Literal Is True
questions.stem: In a CP-SAT model, a feeder's load must be at most 70 unless the feeder is on backup (Boolean b is true on backup); on backup the load has no such limit. Which line states that rule?

options.says: Right: the row holds exactly when b is false, so off backup the limit applies and on backup it is dropped.
This enforces the limit only on backup, the opposite of the rule.
This forces the load above 70 on backup instead of leaving it free.
This forces the load above 70 off backup, where the rule caps it at 70.

questions.heading: Use a Tight Big-M When the Bounds Are Known, an Indicator When They Are Not
questions.stem: A switched row's left side contains a continuous variable that has no finite upper bound anywhere in the model, and the model is solved with SCIP. What should you write, and why?

options.text: A big-M row with M = 1e6, since one huge number covers any bound
options.says: With no finite bound no M is valid for every plan, and a huge M also leaks through the tolerance.

options.text: An indicator constraint, since a valid M needs a bound to come from
options.says: Right: the bound rule gives no M, and the implication is still correct.

options.text: A big-M row with M read off the bounds, since the bounds fix an M
options.says: An infinite upper bound gives no finite M.

options.text: An indicator constraint, since it always solves faster than big-M
options.says: Neither form is always faster; with good bounds the lesson says to measure both on your data.
